title: Define a callback function before using it with map
description:
Define a call function before map, filter or reduce, see examples.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as double_numbers(numbers), which first defines a named callback function that doubles a number and then uses map() with that named callback (not a lambda) to double every number in numbers, returning the result as a list.
hints: Before calling map(), define a normal, named function (with def) that takes one number and returns double that number.
map() takes that function reference (no parentheses after its name) as its first argument and the iterable as its second.
Wrap map(double, numbers) in list(...) so you return a concrete list instead of a lazy map object.
expected_behavior: Returns a new list where each number from the input list has been doubled, computed by defining a named callback function first and passing it to map().
explanation: Defining the callback with def first (instead of inline as a lambda) makes it reusable and named; map() then applies that named function to every item and list() forces the lazy map object into a concrete list.
